question: Can description-logic concept induction over a large Wikipedia-derived class hierarchy automatically generate and statistically test semantic labels for individual hidden units of an ordinary pretrained CNN?

key_findings.claim: The pipeline generates open-vocabulary-style unit hypotheses by combining activation extremes, image object annotations, and ontology induction.
key_findings.evidence: For each of 64 units in a ResNet50V2 dense layer, images above 80% of the unit maximum become positive examples and images below 20% become negative. ADE20K object annotations are exact-string mapped into an approximately two-million-class Wikipedia hierarchy, and ECII returns a high-coverage description-logic concept or conjunction as the proposed unit label.

key_findings.claim: Most selected labels show a reproducible activation association on held-out images retrieved by their words.
key_findings.evidence: Twenty labels pass a confirmation rule on 80% of newly Google-retrieved images. On the reserved 20%, Mann-Whitney tests reject equal target/non-target activation for 19 of 20 labels at p<0.05, with 17 at p<1e-5; examples include crosswalk, mountain-and-bushes, fireplace-and-coffee-table, road-and-car, and skyscraper.

key_findings.claim: The confirmation criterion tests sensitivity but explicitly ignores specificity, allowing weak explanations to be called confirmed.
key_findings.evidence: A label is confirmed whenever at least 80% of target-search images strongly activate its unit, regardless of activation on non-target images. Consequently central-reservation images activate unit 43 at 97.5% but other-label images at 85.42%; footboard-and-chain is 84.38% versus 66.41%, and slope is 91.43% versus 68.85%. Statistical separation does not make these labels selective detectors.

key_findings.claim: The evaluation establishes association with search-query image sets, not a causal or exhaustive neuron interpretation.
key_findings.evidence: Google Images supplies validation examples using the hypothesized phrase itself, and non-targets are images retrieved for the other selected phrases. Search ranking, dataset co-occurrence, near duplicates, style, and shared scene context can separate these groups. No intervention adds/removes the concept, no segmentation-localization check tests where activation arises, and no prediction mediation or causal ablation is performed.

key_findings.claim: The nominal two-million-class search is heavily constrained by existing manual annotations and hierarchy reachability.
key_findings.evidence: Images enter the knowledge base only through ADE20K object labels that exact-match Wikipedia classes; richer segmentation is unused, but object annotation is still required. ECII can primarily return annotated concepts, their ancestors, and conjunctions supported by those links, so the method is not label-free and cannot discover visual properties absent from the annotation ontology, such as color, texture, geometry, or spatial relations.

key_findings.claim: Breadth claims are premature because only one small late dense layer, one model, and one ten-class scene task are analyzed.
key_findings.evidence: The study inspects 64 individual units after a dense layer of one ResNet50V2 fine-tuned on 6,187 ADE20K images from ten selected scene categories. Convolutional layers, distributed unit ensembles, other architectures, datasets, seeds, tasks, and safety-relevant behaviors are explicitly left for future work.

method.core_idea: Treat highly and weakly activating images as positive and negative ontology instances, induce a logical class expression that separates them, then test that phrase on newly retrieved images.
method.mechanism: Fine-tune a ten-way ADE20K scene classifier and record activations of its 64-unit dense layer on 1,370 annotated images. Link each image to exact-matching Wikipedia-derived object classes. For each active unit, run heuristic description-logic concept induction on extreme-activation sets and keep the highest-coverage concept. Retrieve up to 200 Google JPEGs per phrase, use 80% for an 80%-activation confirmation threshold, and use the remaining 20% for target-versus-other-label Mann-Whitney tests.
assumptions: Individual dense units, rather than distributed directions or ensembles, carry stable human concepts.
ADE20K object annotations and the Wikipedia hierarchy contain the causal visual properties driving each unit.
Exact lexical mapping connects annotations to the correct ontology senses.
Google image results are independent, representative concept examples rather than query- and ranking-biased samples.
A high target activation rate plus distributional separation is sufficient evidence for a meaningful explanation.
Maximum-relative thresholds transfer across labels despite differing unit distributions and outliers.

techniques.role: Creates positive and negative example sets for each hidden unit.
Supplies a large structured vocabulary and superclass relationships.
Heuristically proposes atomic or conjunctive description-logic labels from annotated examples.
Acquires new phrase-conditioned images for a second-stage activation test.
Tests whether target-query activations rank above activations for other selected queries.

evaluations.setting: Six ImageNet backbones fine-tuned for ten ADE20K scene classes
evaluations.result: ResNet50V2 is selected with 87.60% training and 86.46% validation accuracy; other candidates range from 26.56% to 53.57% validation except this model.
evaluations.baseline: VGG16, InceptionV3, ResNet50, ResNet101, and ResNet152V2

evaluations.setting: Sixty-four ResNet50V2 dense units on 1,370 annotated ADE20K images
evaluations.metric: ECII coverage for the top induced class expression
evaluations.result: Activated-unit hypotheses have reported coverage above 0.96; twenty pass the later target-image activation confirmation in the main analysis.

evaluations.setting: Held-out 20% of Google Image results for each of twenty confirmed phrases
evaluations.metric: Strong-activation rates, mean/median activation, Mann-Whitney z-score and p-value
evaluations.result: Nineteen of twenty target-versus-other-query comparisons are significant at p<0.05, but non-target strong activation ranges as high as 85.42% and one building label is not significant.
evaluations.baseline: Images retrieved for the other confirmed phrases

evaluations.setting: Appendix variations over positive/negative thresholds and second/third ECII responses
evaluations.metric: Number and activation rates of confirmed labels
evaluations.result: Several cutoff definitions yield broadly similar confirmation patterns; lower-ranked responses also produce significant associations, indicating polysemanticity or incomplete top-label descriptions.

limitations: Only one 64-unit dense layer of one fine-tuned ResNet50V2 and one ten-class ADE20K subset is studied.
The method needs manually annotated objects and exact lexical ontology links; it is not annotation-free.
Google search results introduce semantic, ranking, duplication, copyright, style, and temporal reproducibility confounds.
Confirmation ignores false positives, and several accepted labels have very high non-target activation.
No comparison to Network Dissection, compositional neuron explanations, CLIP-Dissect, TCAV, or human-written labels is run.
P-values are not corrected for label selection, multiple units, multiple ECII responses, or explored threshold variants.
Association is not tested with controlled counterfactuals, segmentation overlap, causal ablation, or downstream prediction mediation.
The hierarchy lacks many low-level visual, relational, counting, and stylistic properties likely to drive units.
Individual units cannot capture distributed and polysemantic representations; ensemble search is deferred.
failure_modes: A generally high-activation unit receives a plausible but nonspecific label because confirmation ignores non-target rate.
Google query style or scene context, rather than the named object, drives the activation difference.
An ambiguous ADE20K word exact-matches the wrong Wikipedia sense and propagates a false superclass explanation.
The causal feature is an unmodeled color, texture, position, or co-occurring object while the induced label names a correlate.
A polysemantic neuron is reduced to the first high-coverage label, hiding unrelated triggers.
Maximum activation is an outlier, making fixed percentage thresholds unstable across samples or datasets.
Search-engine changes or duplicate results make statistical confirmation irreproducible.
reusable_insights: Structured ontologies can expand neuron-label search beyond a hand-written flat vocabulary and support compositional hypotheses.
Separate hypothesis generation from evaluation data, but also use a truly independent acquisition channel and specificity-aware metrics.
Report target sensitivity and non-target specificity together; statistical significance alone is not explanation quality.
Treat neuron labels as falsifiable hypotheses and validate them with concept interventions, localization, and downstream causal effects.
Multiple high-ranked labels can expose polysemantic units better than forcing one canonical description.
open_questions: Can ontology induction operate on automatically grounded masks or vision-language embeddings without manual object annotations?
Do induced labels survive balanced, curated, deduplicated datasets and controlled add/remove concept interventions?
How should sensitivity, specificity, causal precision, human usefulness, and completeness be combined into one validation protocol?
Can scalable search label sparse directions or neuron ensembles rather than axis-aligned individual units?
How do labels transfer across seeds, architectures, layers, datasets, distribution shift, and adversarial examples?
Can ontology relations reveal when a unit encodes context, relation, or composition rather than an object?

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting Deep Visual Representations via Network Dissection
competitive_landscape.difference: Network Dissection labels units by spatial alignment with a densely annotated vocabulary spanning objects, parts, scenes, textures, materials, and colors and studies architecture/training effects. The target replaces segmentation overlap with logical induction over a much larger hierarchy, but tests only a dense layer and relies on object annotations plus search associations without a direct baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Explanations of Neurons
competitive_landscape.difference: Mu and Andreas already search compositional logical concepts that approximate neuron behavior across vision and language, quantify polysemanticity, connect explanations to task performance, and build adversarial interventions. The target's distinctive element is description-logic deduction over a two-million-class external hierarchy, not compositional neuron explanation itself.

competitive_landscape.title: CLIP-Dissect: Automatic Description of Neuron Representations in Deep Vision Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: CLIP-Dissect uses vision-language similarity to label five ResNet-50 layers in about four minutes without labeled examples, reports last-layer accuracy comparisons, and includes a crowdsourced study. The target offers symbolic hierarchy and conjunction semantics, but needs ADE annotations, analyzes one small layer, and reports neither runtime nor head-to-head label quality.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Large-scale description-logic background knowledge and concept induction can automatically hypothesize and verify meaningful semantic labels for individual CNN hidden neurons without modifying the trained network or restricting explanations to a small predefined category set.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The system induces labels for dense units from activation extremes over ADE20K, confirms twenty with new Google images, and finds statistically higher target-query activations for nineteen on a reserved split, with extensive threshold and lower-ranked-response appendices.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Using a million-scale formal hierarchy as the label generator is a legitimate neuro-symbolic contribution. However, compositional and open-vocabulary automatic neuron labeling were already established. The effective vocabulary is annotation-bounded, and the search-image test validates association more than meaning or causality. High non-target activation, one model/layer/task, ad hoc selection, and missing strong baselines make this a promising proof of concept rather than a systematic verified interpretation method.

reviewer_notes: Read all sixteen pages of the exact indexed manuscript, including the full pipeline, every main and appendix table, all cutoff variants, second/third ECII-response analyses, discussion, and references. Source hashes and page count match fulltext_index.jsonl. Three direct official arXiv primary competitors were checked on 2026-08-23. The audit distinguishes ontology-scale novelty from prior compositional/open-vocabulary labeling and separates statistically significant search-set association from specificity, causal feature identity, and explanation completeness.
